Here is Section 1 of your Form I-9. It is only about you, the employee. Your wife's and daughter's details are not used anywhere on this form.

Section 1. Employee Information and Attestation

[B01] Last Name (Family Name): SURNAME_P1
[B02] First Name (Given Name): GIVEN_P1
[B03] Middle Initial (if any): MIDDLE_P1
      By hand: the form wants the initial only. Keep the first letter of your middle name and delete the rest.
[B04] Other Last Names Used (if any): N/A
[B05] Address (Street Number and Name): NEEDS-YOU
[B06] Apt. Number (if any): NEEDS-YOU
[B07] City or Town: NEEDS-YOU (presumably Seattle, but enter what your address actually says)
[B08] State: NEEDS-YOU (WA if the address is in Washington)
[B09] ZIP Code: NEEDS-YOU
      Your new US address is not saved in mdoc, so fill B05 to B09 yourself. Don't use your saved home address (ADDRESS_P1): the I-9 asks for where you live now in the US.
[B10] Date of Birth (mm/dd/yyyy): DATE_P1
      By hand: this is your date of birth as printed in your passport. Rewrite it in US order, month/day/year with four digits for the year (for example, the 3rd of May becomes 05/03/...). Don't leave it in the day-first order passports usually use.
[B11] U.S. Social Security Number: leave blank
      You don't have an SSN yet. That's fine, because the SSN is optional on the I-9 unless your employer uses E-Verify. If they do, tell HR you've applied for (or will apply for) a number. They will add it once you get it. Don't make one up or write something like "applied" in the boxes.
[B12] Employee's Email Address: optional. NEEDS-YOU if you want to give one. No email address is saved in mdoc.
[B13] Employee's Telephone Number: PHONE_P1
      This field is optional. If your saved number isn't the one you'll use in the US, put your US number here yourself or leave it blank.

Citizenship or immigration status:
[B14] [X] 4. An alien authorized to work until (exp. date, if any): 01/15/2029
      Leave boxes 1, 2 and 3 empty.

[B15] Enter ONE of these (you only need one):
      Foreign Passport Number and Country of Issuance: ID_P1, India
      Leave USCIS A-Number and Form I-94 Admission Number empty.
      Note: L-1 holders usually don't have an A-Number. If you'd rather give your I-94 Admission Number, that is equally fine, but it isn't saved in mdoc (NEEDS-YOU). In that case, leave the passport line empty.

[B16] Signature of Employee: sign by hand (or with the employer's e-signature system)
[B17] Today's Date (mm/dd/yyyy): the date you sign, written by hand
      Sign no later than your first day of work, but not before you accepted the job offer.

Preparer and/or Translator Certification: leave it blank if you fill in and sign Section 1 yourself.

Before you submit, check these:
- The expiry date in B14 (01/15/2029) should match the "Admit Until Date" on your I-94 record. If they differ, use the I-94 date.
- On or before your third day of work, your employer will need to see your documents for Section 2. For an L-1 that is usually your Indian passport plus your I-94 showing L-1 status (a List A document). Your passport is valid until 4 June 2029, so it is unexpired.
